newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks bounce at open after Dow rides storm.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks bounce at open after Dow rides storm.

text.p: Australian shares sprang back early on Monday after being oversold on Friday following cautionary comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
At 10.25 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 25.3 points up at 2,339.2. The December share index was up 35 points at 2,338 and at a 1.2 point discount to the underlying index.
Although the Dow was down more than 140 points at one stage on Friday, a mixed employment report eased fears that the Fed could raise short term interest rates.
"The market bounced as predicted but buying has still been a little cautious," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said that although BHP and major bank stocks found early support, these stocks were still well away from their closing levels on Thursday.
"There is still some room for bargain hunters and they could well be ain gain this afternoon if they are confident enough that Wall Street will retain its resolve tonight," the dealer said.
Industrial issues were fairing better than resources, primarily due to the strong performance of the bank sector which was among the worst affected by selling on Friday.
